To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stomatal traits are associated with yield and QTL controlling stomatal traits are located in regions that overlap with QTL for yield.
stomatal traits are important determinants of wheat yield under drought and that the genetics of stomatal density and size are linked to yield in wheat.

1) stomatal size and number are genetically correlated in wheat; 2) stomatal traits are heritable; 3) some stomatal traits are associated with yield under water-limited conditions; 4) stomatal traits may be used as a proxy for yield QTL.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding stomatal function, and its relationship to yield in wheat under drought, and has the potential to provide a basis for the development of wheat varieties with increased yield stability under low rainfall conditions.
identifying the genetic basis of stomatal traits in relation to yield in wheat grown under field and controlled drought conditions.
the identification of QTL for stomata traits in wheat, and the genetic relationships between stomata traits and yield in water deficit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QTL identified in this study could be used to identify candidate genes to accelerate the cloning of yield QQL under drought.
the stomatal size and number per unit leaf area are two important traits for improving yield in wheat under water limited conditions.
stomata are a complex trait that can affect yield under water deficit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic variation of stomatal traits in the flag leaf is an important component in the genetic architecture of wheat yield under drought.
we found that stomatal traits are not directly correlated to yield, but that they can be used as a proxy for a target QTL.
stomatal traits can be used as a proxy for yield in wheat under water limited conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stomatal traits can be used as a proxy for yield QTL and that the genetic basis for stomatal traits is complex.
stomata can be used as a proxy for yield in wheat breeding programs and that the genetic control of stomata is complex.
stomatal traits may be useful as an indirect selection criterion for yield in breeding for wheat under drought conditions.
